title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Departure Board. Keep it, take the pick or an alternate, keep today's look refined (the category standard), or re-roll.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: Solari split-flap station boards, and the flip panels of 70s game-show survey boards
options.thesis: Every quiz is a timetable: questions, room codes and scores arrive on clattering split-flap boards.
options.viewport: One black board fills the view. It reads NOW BOARDING · 10 QUESTIONS · ANY CATEGORY, with a single yellow Play key. A 5-flap room code slot sits beside it, and the tiles flip in as it loads.
options.risk: Flip motion gets tiring on long text, so it's limited to codes, numbers and short labels. The question text sits still and readable, and reduced-motion is respected.

raised.raise: Signal yellow appears only on 'now': the current question, your leaderboard row, the one primary action.
Every setting is its own labeled switch on the board. Difficulty and type are segmented flap selectors, not dropdowns.
Correct, wrong and pending are carried by glyph and form (a ✓ tile, a ✕ tile, a ticking pending flap), never by colour alone.
Question progress is one unbroken row of cells with a lit 'now' cell. Tap any cell to jump.
Question numbers live in a fixed platform-number column, a strict numbered margin like a platform board.
Boards hang as separate modules on the hall wall with clear gaps between them, never cards nested in cards.

options.label: Answer Sheet
options.lineage: machine-scored bubble answer sheets and No. 2 pencils
options.thesis: Every question is a row of A–D bubbles you fill in pencil, and the scoring machine marks it.
options.viewport: A printed answer form: a name box and settings as form fields at the top, the current question with four big bubbles, and timing marks down the edge.
options.risk: It's the most obvious quiz reference, where most runs in this category would land, and it carries some exam-stress baggage.

options.label: Monochrome Product Page
options.thesis: A neutral scale with one accent, where every claim is paired with proof.
options.viewport: A two-weight sans on a strict grid, with ghost buttons.
options.case: Loses identification: it reads as the corporate SaaS look you ruled out. It also adds no clarity over the board.
options.kept: The discipline of rationing one accent to the moments that matter.

options.label: Cassette Deck Fascia
options.thesis: Settings as chrome toggles, with score as an amber LED ladder.
options.viewport: One fascia with bolted panel zones.
options.case: Players don't recognise hi-fi gear as trivia, and the toggles are clear but gimmicky at quiz scale.
options.kept: Every function gets its own labeled physical control.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: State carried by line form (height, dash, doubling) on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with the open item blooming above it.
options.case: Too abstract for trivia players, and it costs clarity on the first read.
options.kept: State through form rather than hue, which is exactly what AA needs.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: The quiz as a 16-step row with a chase light on 'now'.
options.viewport: The step row as the page's single unbroken line.
options.case: Music gear isn't trivia's world, but the step row is a very clear progress navigator.
options.kept: One unbroken row with a lit 'now' cell.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One vermilion sheet folded through numbered steps.
options.viewport: Square diagram with a numbered margin column.
options.case: Unrelated to trivia and slower to parse.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Content cut as blocks of weather with blue voids between.
options.viewport: Sections stacked like cut blocks with deep gaps between them.
options.case: Dreamlike, with no link to trivia. It hurts both identification and clarity.
options.kept: Stacked modules with clear gaps between them.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern quiz app, executed impeccably. It's the closest to today's look, with the gradients, glows and emoji removed.
canonCard.viewport: A large question with four colored answer tiles and a slim progress bar.
canonCard.risk: It looks like every other quiz app by design.
